items.content_html:
Specification title

Extend CSP script-src hashes

Specification or proposal URL (if available)

w3c/webappsec-csp@main...carlosjoan91:webappsec-csp:main

Explainer URL (if available)

https://github.com/explainers-by-googlers/script-src-v2/blob/main/README.md

Proposal author(s)

@carlosjoan91, @meacer

MDN URL

No response

Caniuse.com URL

No response

Bugzilla URL

No response

Mozillians who can provide input

No response

WebKit standards-position

Not created yet

Other information

This feature adds two new prefixes to hashes in script-src directives (url- and eval-) and a new keyword (strict-dynamic-url).

Note that we originally intended to add these to a new directive called script-src-v2. At the moment, we are adding them to the existing script-src directive only, but the explainer and other text may still refer to script-src-v2.

url- hash prefix

This enables allowlisting scripts by their URL's hash:

Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'url-sha256-SHA256("https://example.com/script.js")';
<script src="https://example.com/script.js"></script>

eval- hash prefix

eval- prefix enables allowlisting eval'ed scripts by their hash, obviating the need to use unsafe-eval:

Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'eval-sha256-SHA256("console.log('Hello World')';
<script>
eval("console.log('Hello World')");
</script>

strict-dynamic-url

One of the main goals of this change is to keep compatibility with old browsers. To do this, it introduces a new keyword called strict-dynamic-url. This keyword allows using url hashes in a single, combined policy in both old and new user agents like so:

Content-Security-Policy: script-src https: 'unsafe-inline' 'strict-dynamic-url' url-hash-EXRatbw5eQNZwUCOApq3KI4p5S8ou8jvXBOolnXEg0k='

Old user agents will treat this policy as https: 'unsafe-inline', whereas new user agents will treat it as 'strict-dynamic-url' url-hash-EXRatbw5eQNZwUCOApq3KI4p5S8ou8jvXBOolnXEg0k='. Using strict-dynamic wouldn't work here, as it would cause old user agents to ignore the 'https:' source.
items.title: Extend CSP script-src hashes

Support "write"-only permission mode in FileSystem/FileSystemAccess API

Specification or proposal URL (if available)

No response

Proposal author(s)

Caniuse.com URL

No response

Bugzilla URL

Mozillians who can provide input

No response

WebKit standards-position

WebKit/standards-positions#534

Other information

The File System Access API defines two access modes for file system entries: "read" and "readwrite". These modes are used when querying or requesting permission to an entry.

An issue with the current model is that operations requiring only file system modification, such as FileSystemHandle.remove(), are forced to request broad "readwrite" permission. This behavior poses some unnecessary security risks. Add a new "write"-only access mode and adjust the existing APIs would solve the issue.
items.title: Support "write"-only permission mode in FileSystem/FileSystemAccess API

This adds border-*-radius short hands. For example the new border-top-radius would be a shorthand for border-top-left-radius and border-top-right-radius.

This helps to avoid the awkward current alternative shorthand which is border-radius: 24px 24px 0 0;. It's often difficult for devs to remember the order of corners in the shorthand. And declaring the zeros for corners you don't want to touch seems like extra work we shouldn't really need to do.

Logical equivalence are also included.

items.content_html:
Specification title

Support for width and height as css attributes on use element

Specification or proposal URL (if available)

https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG2/struct.html#UseElement

Explainer URL (if available)

No response

Proposal author(s)

No response

MDN URL

No response

Caniuse.com URL

No response

Bugzilla URL

No response

Mozillians who can provide input

No response

WebKit standards-position

No response

Other information

The SVG 2.0 specification introduces support for applying CSS width and height to element, enabling more flexible and consistent styling of reused SVG content. This enhancement allows developers to control element sizing through CSS, improving responsiveness and aligning SVG behavior with modern web styling practices.

With this feature enabled, the following two HTML snippets will now render identically:

Using CSS Properties on the element [1]:

<svg width="100px" height="100px">
 <defs>
    <symbol id="sym" width="80" height="80">
      <rect width="100" height="100" fill="green"/>
    </symbol>
  </defs>
  <use href="#sym" style="width:40px; height:40px"/>
</svg>

Using presentation attributes on the element [2]:

<svg width="100px" height="100px">
 <defs>
    <symbol id="sym" width="80" height="80">
      <rect width="100" height="100" fill="green"/>
    </symbol>
  </defs>
  <use href="#sym" width="40" height="40"/>
</svg>

Note that in Firefox currently the [1] example gives incorrect result, that is, width and height as styles are not applied on use element.
items.title: [SVG] Support for width and height as css attributes on <use> element
